BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r2.claim: “When he saw a fire” marks the time of the account.

BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r3.speaker: السهيلي
BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r3.claim: Al-Suhayli identifies Moses’ wife as Ṣafūriyya, daughter of Shuʿayb.
BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r3.anchor: وقال السهيلي صفورياء بنت شعيب عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r4.claim: Moses asked to leave Midian to visit his mother and Aaron in Egypt; on a dark, cold, snowy Friday night his wife gave birth near Ṭuwa, his fire-striker sounded but produced no flame.
BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r4.anchor: فاستأذن منه في الخروج من مدين لزيارة أمه وأخيه هارون في مصر

BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r5.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r5.claim: Another account says Moses’ jealousy led him to travel with his family at night and leave by day, causing him to lose the company and route.
BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r5.anchor: وقيل كان موسى رجلا غيورا يصحب الناس بالليل ويفارقهم بالنهار

BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r6.claim: He saw a distant fire to the left of the road, thought it belonged to shepherds, and hoped to bring back a flame.
BURSEVI:v5p283#3/r6.anchor: فبينما هو في ذلك إذ رأى نارا من بعيد على يسار الطريق من جانب الطور

BURSEVI:v5p284/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BURSEVI:v5p284/r1.claim: Most commentators say Moses saw divine light rather than fire, which was called fire because that is what he thought it was.
BURSEVI:v5p284/r1.anchor: قال أكثر المفسرين : إن الذي رآه موسى لم يكن نارا بل كان نور الرب تعالى ذكر بلفظ النار

BURSEVI:v5p284/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284/r2.speaker: الإمام
BURSEVI:v5p284/r2.claim: The author endorses the view that Moses truly saw fire, so his report was truthful; prophets cannot lie.
BURSEVI:v5p284/r2.anchor: وقال الإمام الصحيح أنه رأى نارا ليكون صادقا في خبره إذ الكذب لا يجوز على الأنبياء

BURSEVI:v5p284/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284/r3.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v5p284/r3.claim: Some Sufis say God manifested in the form Moses desired, fire, to draw his attention; a different form might have made him turn away.
BURSEVI:v5p284/r3.anchor: لما كانت النار بغية موسى تجلى الله له في صورة مطلوبة المجازي ليقبل عليه

BURSEVI:v5p284/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p284/r4.claim: The poem says Moses saw what he sought as fire, not recognizing God manifested in light and speech.
BURSEVI:v5p284/r4.anchor:
كنار موسى يراها عين حاجته
وهو الاله ولكن ليس يدريه

BURSEVI:v5p284/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p284/r5.claim: Moses hopes to find someone to guide him because fires often have people around them; hudā can mean a guide or one possessing guidance.
BURSEVI:v5p284/r5.anchor: {أو أجد على النار هدى} هاديا يدلني على الطريق لأن النار قلما تخلو من أهل لها

BURSEVI:v5p284/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p284/r6.claim: The two alternatives joined by “or” need not exclude one another; ʿalā indicates people standing around or over the fire.
BURSEVI:v5p284/r6.anchor: وكلمة أو في الموضعين لمنع الخلو دون منع الجمع ومعنى الاستعلاء في على

QASHANI:20:6-12/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:6-12/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:6-12/r4.claim: The fire is the Holy Spirit kindling light in human souls, seen through insight illumined by guidance; Moses's family are psychic faculties he tells to stay still as senses quiet for the sacred journey.
QASHANI:20:6-12/r4.anchor: هي روح القدس التي ينقدح منها النور في النفوس الإنسانية

QASHANI:20:6-12/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:6-12/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:6-12/r5.claim: The firebrand is a luminous connection benefiting the faculties; alternatively, finding a guide means gaining knowledge and gnosis that lead to truth through contact with the Holy Spirit.
QASHANI:20:6-12/r5.anchor: أي: هيئة نورية اتصالية ينتفع بها كلكم فيتنور وتصير ذاته فضيلة

QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r6.claim: The Qur’an often follows mention of Muhammad with Moses; God showed Moses the fire to draw him away from his family, though the fire itself was not the true aim.
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r6.anchor: ألاح له النار حتى أخرجه من أهله يطلبها ، وكان المقصود إخراجه من بينهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r7.claim: Moses approached while the fire receded, and left his family to seek a firebrand for them despite the danger of the valley.
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r7.anchor: فكان موسى عليه السلام يدنو والنار تنأى ، وقال لأهله

QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r8.claim: One account says Moses was seized by agitation at the sight of the fire and could not hold himself back from going out.
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r8.anchor: استولى على موسى عند رؤيته النار الانزعاج ، فلم يتمالك حتى خرج

QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r9.claim: Moses found a tree burning from end to end, but it would not yield a flame; the fire illuminated hearts rather than bodies.
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r9.anchor: هذه النار تضيء ولكن لا تعطي لأحد منها شعلة . يا موسى هذه النار تحرق القلوب لا النفوس

QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r10.claim: As Moses tried to take a flame, he heard God’s call and recognized it by its ordered structure and composition.
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r10.anchor: علم موسى أنه كلام الحق - سبحانه - لما سمع فيه الترتيب والتنظيم والتركيب

QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r11.claim: Another view says God identified His speech to Moses through special inspiration, without inference.
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r11.anchor: بتعريف خصه الحق - سبحانه - به من حيث الإلهام دون نوع من الاستدلال

FARRA:v2p175/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p175/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p175/r1.claim: A qabs is a piece of fire carried at the tip of a stick or reed.
FARRA:v2p175/r1.anchor: القبس مثل النار في طرف العود أو في القصبة

FARRA:v2p175/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p175/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p175/r2.claim: هُدًى means a guide; the verbal noun stands in for the active participle, and Moses had lost the way.
FARRA:v2p175/r2.anchor: يعني هاديا. فأجزأ المصدر من الهادي

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#4/r1.claim: آنست نارا means I saw a fire; elsewhere the same verb means I knew or recognized, as in the orphan verse.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#4/r1.anchor: أبصرت. وتكون في موضع آخر: علمت

NAHHAS:v3p33/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p33/r4.speaker: حمزة
NAHHAS:v3p33/r4.claim: Hamza reads the original form, also in al-Qasas; it follows the dialect of مررت بهو, retaining the original wāw, though this departs from his usual practice in these two places.
NAHHAS:v3p33/r4.anchor: وهذا على لغة من قال مررت بهو يا هذا فجاء به على الأصل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p38/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p38/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p38/r2.claim: The verb governing id is implicit in ḥadīth, roughly asking what Moses did when he saw the fire.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r1.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih reports that Moses asked Shuʿayb to return to his mother, then left with his family; on a cold night a child was born, his fire-starting failed, and he saw fire to the left of the road.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r1.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه استأذن موسى شعيبا عليهما السلام في الرجوع إلى والدته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r2.claim: Commentators say Moses saw a light, but the account reports his assumption that it was a fire; he told his wife to wait where she was.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون رأى نورا ولكن اخبر بما كان في ظن موسى فقال لأهله يعنى امرأته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r3.speaker: حمزة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r3.claim: Hamza reads the hāʾ in li-ahlihi with ḍamma here and in the parallel phrasing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة لأهله امكثوا بضم الهاء ها هنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r4.claim: Al-Farra says ānastu means “I found”; Ibn Qutayba says it means “I saw.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r4.anchor: قال الفراء اني وجدت يقال هل آنست احدا اي وجدت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines a qabas as fire taken at the end of a stick or wick.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272/r5.anchor: هو ما أخذته من النار في رأس عود أو في رأس فتيلة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272#2/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272#2/r1.claim: Al-Farra says Moses meant “a guide,” using the verbal noun form huda for a guide.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272#2/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says ʿalā here can mean “at,” “with,” or “by.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن الأنبارى يجوز ان تكون ﴿ على ﴾ ها هنا بمعنى ﴿ عند ﴾ وبمعنى مع وبمعنى الباء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272#2/r3.claim: Commentators say Moses had lost the road; al-Zajjaj adds that he had lost the water and hoped to find someone to guide him to the road or water.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p272#2/r3.anchor: ضل عن الماء فرجا أن يجد من يهديه الطريق أو يدله على الماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p275#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p275#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p275#2/r1.claim: After completing his sheep-tending term with his father-in-law, Moses heads toward Egypt with his wife after over ten years away; on a cold, dark, stormy night he loses the way, fails to light his flint, and sees fire on a mountain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p275#2/r1.anchor: بعد ما قضى موسى الأجل الذي كان بينه وبين صهره في رعاية الغنم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p275#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p275#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p275#2/r2.claim: Moses hopes to bring a flame or ember; 28:29 adds a glowing brand and warmth, indicating darkness and cold.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p275#2/r2.anchor: من نار. وفي الآية الأخرى: {أو جذوة من النار}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276/r1.claim: Moses was cold with his family and had lost the road; he seeks someone to guide him, or else will bring back fire for them to kindle.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276/r1.anchor: من يهديني إلى الطريق. وكانوا شاتين وضلوا الطريق

JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.claim: On the preceding question about divine istiwāʾ, the author says the sounder view of Abū ʿAlī is that it means power; the Kullābī account of an act or attribute called istiwāʾ is unintelligible.
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.anchor: وإن كان الأصح ما ذهب إليه أبو علي أن المراد به الاقتدار

JISHUMI:v6p4638/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r2.speaker: حمزة
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r2.claim: Hamzah reads the hāʾ of “for his family” with ḍamma by transferring the hamzah’s vowel; the others read it with kasra for two adjacent sukūns.
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة: لأهله امكثوا بضم الهاء، نقل حركة الهمزة إلى الهاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r2.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r2.claim: Moses saw what appeared to him as fire, while to God it was light; Muqātil says the night was a winter Friday.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r2.anchor: وكانت عند موسى نارا , وعند الله نورا , قال مقاتل : وكانت ليلة الجمعة في الشتاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r3.claim: Amkuthū means stay; iqāma implies continuing residence, while mukth is temporary.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r3.anchor: أي أقيموا . والفرق بين المكث والإقامة أن الإقامة تدوم والمكث لا يدوم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r4.claim: Ānastu nāran may mean “I saw a fire” or “I sensed something by a fire.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r4.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : رأيت نارا . والثاني : إني آنست بنار

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r5.claim: A qabaṣ is a piece of fire to warm yourselves with.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r6.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r6.claim: Guidance at the fire may mean a guide to show Moses the way.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r7.claim: Guidance may instead mean a sign by which to find the road; after Moses left, his family stayed three days until a village shepherd found them, and they lived in the village forty years.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p394/r7.anchor: علامة أستدل بها على الطريق . وكانوا قد ضلوا عنه فمكثوا بمكانهم بعد ذهاب موسى ثلاثة أيام

MUJAHID:v1p393#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p393#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p393#3/r1.claim: Moses hopes to find guidance to the road by the fire.
MUJAHID:v1p393#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ أو أجد على النار هدى ﴾ يهديه الطريق

MUQATIL:20:9-12/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:9-12/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:9-12/r1.claim: On a winter Friday night in the Holy Land, lost Moses saw fire, told his wife and child to wait, and hoped to bring a flame for warmth or find a guide; it was the Lord’s light, and angelic praise frightened him before God gave him calm.
MUQATIL:20:9-12/r1.anchor: ليلة الجمعة في الشتاء بأرض المقدسة، { فقال لأهله } يعني امرأته وولده { امكثوا } مكانكم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r1.claim: The time phrase may modify an omitted event or serve as the object of recall; tradition says Moses left with his family after asking Shuʿayb to visit his mother, during a dark snowy night after a birth, loss of the road and livestock, and failure to kindle fire; the apparent fire was light.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r1.anchor: روى أن موسى عليه السلام استأذن شعيبا في الخروج إلى أمه وخرج بأهله فولد له ابن في الطريق في ليلة مظلمة مثلجة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r2.claim: Amkuthū means remain in your place; ānastu means I saw, from perceiving something that offers comfort.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ فقال لأهله امكثوا ﴾ اقيموا في مكانكم ﴿ إني آنست ﴾ ابصرت ﴿ نارا ﴾ والايناس رؤية شيء يؤنس به

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r3.claim: Moses frames his hope cautiously so he does not promise what he has not yet confirmed.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r3.anchor: بني الأمر على الرجاء لئلا يعد ما ليس يستيقن

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r4.claim: Qabas means an ember carried on a stick or a wick/tinder.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r4.anchor: ﴿ بقبس ﴾ نار مقتبس في رأس عود أو فتبلة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r5.claim: Hudā can mean a guide or people who guide him to the road; على marks the elevated place where people stand by the fire.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#3/r5.anchor: ﴿ أو أجد على النار هدى ﴾ ذوي هدى أو قوما يهدونني الطريق ومعنى الاستعلاء في على النار

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and others place the scene after Moses completed his term and left Midian for Egypt; he lost the route on a dark night.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r4.anchor: هذا حين قضى الأجل وسار بأهله وهو مقبل من مدين يريد مصر

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r5.claim: The account says Moses was protective of his wife, traveling with people at night and separately by day so they would not see her; by God's decree he became separated from the group.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r5.anchor: وكان موسى عليه السلام رجلا غيورا، يصحب الناس بالليل ويفارقهم بالنهار

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r6.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r6.claim: Muqatil says it was a winter Friday night.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r7.speaker: وهب بن منبه
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r7.claim: Wahb says Moses asked Shuʿayb to let him return to his mother, then left with family and flock; a son was born in freezing snow, the route was lost, the flock scattered, and his fire striker failed.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r7.anchor: استأذن موسى شعيبا في الرجوع إلى والدته فأذن له

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r8.claim: Moses noticed a distant fire on the left side of the road and told his family to remain where they were; amkuthū means stay.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses saw the fire in a jujube tree and marveled that its green beauty remained despite the fire's heat and brightness.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r9.anchor: فإذا النار في شجرة عناب، فوقف متعجبا من حسن ذلك الضوء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r10.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r10.claim: Al-Mahdawī relates that the fire appeared in a thorn tree, receded as Moses approached, then drew near after he felt fear, and God spoke from the tree.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r10.anchor: فرأى النار فيما روي وهي في شجرة من العليق

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r11.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r11.claim: Al-Māwardī distinguishes what Moses perceived as fire from what God made it: light.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r11.anchor: الماوردي: كانت عند موسى نارا، وكانت عند الله تعالى نورا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r12.speaker: حمزة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r12.claim: Hamza reads li-ahlihi amkuthū with a ḍamma on the hāʾ, also in al-Qaṣaṣ.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r12.anchor: وقرأ حمزة «لأهله امكثوا» بضم الهاء، وكذا في «القصص»

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r13.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r13.claim: Al-Naḥḥās explains Hamza's reading as preserving the pronoun's original form, an allowed dialect, though Hamza departs from his usual practice only in these two places.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r13.anchor: قال النحاس وهذا على لغة من قال: مررت بهو يا رجل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r14.claim: Moses says amkuthū rather than aqīmū because إقامة implies permanence, while remaining may be temporary.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r14.anchor: وقال: «امكثوا» ولم يقل أقيموا، لأن الإقامة تقتضي الدوام، والمكث ليس كذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r15.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-10/r15.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī glosses ānastu as I saw.

SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r1.claim: إذ رأى may be governed by the preceding account, by an implied اذكر according to Abu al-Baqa, or by an implied following verb according to al-Zamakhshari.
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون منصوبا بالحديث وهو الظاهر. ويجوز أن ينتصب ب " اذكر " مقدرا، كما قاله أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r2.claim: هل retains its ordinary confirmatory-question meaning, though it is also said to mean قد or negation.
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r2.anchor: و " هل " على بابها من كونها استفهام تقرير، وقيل: بمعنى قد، وقيل: بمعنى النفي

SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r3.speaker: حمزة
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r3.claim: Hamza reads لأهله امكثوا with a ḍamma on ه; it is the original Hijazi dialect, while Abu al-Baqa attributes it to vowel assimilation.
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r3.anchor: وقرأ " لأهله امكثوا " بضم الهاء حمزة وقد تقدم أنه الأصل وهو لغة الحجاز

SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r4.claim: آنست means clearly saw; other explanations are found or sensed, the latter being broader than sight, with a poetic witness for sensing a sound.
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r4.anchor: آنست } أي: أبصرت. والإيناس: الإبصار البين، ومنه إنسان العين؛ لأنه يبصر به الأشياء

SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r5.claim: القبس is a flame or burning stick, literally a glowing end on a rod; it is a verbal noun with passive sense like something seized or broken.
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r5.anchor: والقبس: الجذوة من النار، وهي الشعلة في رأس عود أو قصبة ونحوهما. وهو فعل بمعنى مفعول

SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r6.speaker: المبرد
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r6.claim: He distinguishes أقبست for giving knowledge from قبسته for giving fire.
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r6.anchor: ويقال: أقبست الرجل علما وقبسته نارا، ففرقوا بينهما، هذا قول المبرد

SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r7.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r7.claim: He allows فعل and أفعل for both meanings, whether giving knowledge or fire.
SAMIN-DURR:20:10/r7.anchor: وقال الكسائي: إن فعل وأفعل يقالان في المعنيين، فيقال: قبسته نارا وعلما

SAMIN-DURR:20:10#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:10#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:10#2/r1.claim: منها may attach to آتيكم or be a circumstantial phrase qualifying قبس.
SAMIN-DURR:20:10#2/r1.anchor: وقوله { منها } يجوز أن يتعلق/ ب " آتيكم " أو بمحذوف على أنه حال من قبس

SAMIN-DURR:20:10#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:10#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:10#2/r2.claim: Some pause with imāla on هدى, but the better reading avoids imāla because the final alif is generally a substitute for tanwin.
SAMIN-DURR:20:10#2/r2.anchor: وأمال بعضهم ألف " هدى " وقفا. والجيد أن لا تمال لأن الأشهر أنها بدل من التنوين

RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r1.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r1.claim: The commentators relate that Moses asked Shuʿayb to return to his mother, left with his family, had a child on a freezing snowy Friday night, lost the road, and saw a distant fire after his tinder would not catch.
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون : استأذن موسى عليه السلام شعيبا في الرجوع إلى والدته فأذن له فخرج فولد له ابن

RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r2.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses thought the distant light was a shepherd’s fire.
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r2.anchor: قال السدي : ظن أنها نار من نيران الرعاة

RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r3.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r3.claim: Others say Moses saw the fire in a tree, though al-Razi says the Qur’anic wording does not establish that.
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون : إنه عليه السلام رآها في شجرة وليس في لفظ القرآن ما يدل على ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r4.claim: Against the view that Moses merely imagined a fire, al-Razi holds that it was real, so Moses’ report was truthful; lying is impermissible for prophets.
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r4.anchor: والصحيح أنه رأى نارا ليكون صادقا في خبره إذ الكذب لا يجوز على الأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r5.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r5.claim: One classification says worldly fire eats without drinking, green-wood fire drinks without eating, stomach fire does both, and Moses’ fire does neither.
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r5.anchor: نار تأكل ولا تشرب وهي نار الدنيا ، ونار تشرب ولا تأكل وهي نار الشجر

RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r6.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r6.claim: A second classification distinguishes fire with light but no burning (Moses’), burning without light (Hell), both (worldly), and neither (trees).
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r6.anchor: نار لها نور بلا حرقة وهي نار موسى عليه السلام . وثانيها : حرقة بلا نور وهي نار جهنم

RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r7.claim: “His family” may mean his wife, child, and servant together, or only his wife; the plural may reflect the ordinary collective meaning of family or respectful address to one person.
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r7.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون الخطاب للمرأة وولدها والخادم الذي معها ويجوز أن يكون للمرأة وحدها

RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r8.claim: Ānastu means seeing distinctly and without doubt; the associated meanings explain why the word suggests visible humans, in contrast with hidden jinn.
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r8.anchor: والإيناس الإبصار البين الذي لا شبهة فيه ومنه إنسان العين فإنه يبين به الشيء والإنس لظهورهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r9.claim: Moses says “perhaps” because obtaining a firebrand or guidance was still uncertain; this caution shows that he did not promise what he could not guarantee, contrary to the claim that Abraham lied for a good purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r9.anchor: ولما كان الإيناس بالقبس ووجود الهدى مترقبين متوقعين بني الأمر فيهما على الرجاء والطمع

RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r10.claim: A qabas is fire carried on the end of a stick, wick, or similar object; guidance is a source of direction or a sign to follow.
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r10.anchor: والقبس النار المقتبسة في رأس عود أو فتيلة أو غيرهما : { أو أجد على النار هدى }

RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r11.claim: Being “upon” the fire means being on nearby elevated ground or overlooking it, as people gathered around it are above it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p14/r11.anchor: ومعنى الاستعلاء على النار أن أهل النار يستعلون المكان القريب منها

STUDYQURAN:20:10/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:10/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:20:10/r1.claim: Moses encountered God at night in winter after losing his way.
STUDYQURAN:20:10/r1.anchor: Moses’ encounter with God occurred at night, during the winter, when Moses had lost his way (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:20:10/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:10/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:20:10/r2.claim: Moses sought warmth or illumination from the fire he saw.
STUDYQURAN:20:10/r2.anchor: Having seen the fire (Q), he sought warmth or perhaps some means of illumination from it

STUDYQURAN:20:10/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:10/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:10/r3.claim: The fire is said to have been on Horeb, the mountain of God in Exodus; it also symbolizes rising levels of spiritual certainty.
STUDYQURAN:20:10/r3.anchor: It is said that the fire was on Horeb

TAB-FULL:v16p18/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p18/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p18/r1.claim: The account consoles Muhammad amid Quraysh's persecution: God will raise him over them, weaken unbelievers' schemes, and urges perseverance in worship and effort, recalling Moses' ordeals among enemies and Israel.
TAB-FULL:v16p18/r1.anchor: وأنه معليه عليهم، وموهن كيد الكافرين، ويحثه على الجد في أمره

TAB-FULL:v16p18/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p18/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p18/r2.claim: Moses saw the fire on a winter night after losing the way.
TAB-FULL:v16p18/r2.anchor: كان في الشتاء ليلا، وأن موسى كان أضل الطريق

TAB-FULL:v16p18/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p18/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p18/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses had lost the road after completing his term; in winter he saw what he thought was fire, but it was God's light.
TAB-FULL:v16p18/r3.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عباس: كان في الشتاء، ورفعت لهم نار

TAB-FULL:v16p18/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p18/r4.speaker: وهب بن منبه اليماني
TAB-FULL:v16p18/r4.claim: Wahb recounts that Moses routinely kindled a fire for his family and flock, but on the honored night lost the route, his flint failed, and he saw the fire after repeated attempts.
TAB-FULL:v16p18/r4.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه اليماني، قال: لما قضى موسى الأجل

TAB-FULL:v16p18/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p18/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p18/r5.claim: Ānastu means I found or perceived; the word derives from uns, and Arabs used a proverb about perception after looking out.

TAB-FULL:v16p20/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r1.claim: A qabas is a flame carried on the end of a stick or reed; Moses wanted it so his family could warm themselves.
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r1.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، عن وهب بن منبه، {لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس} [طه: 10] قال: بقبس تصطلون

TAB-FULL:v16p20/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r2.claim: Wahb says Moses sought a firebrand with which the family could warm themselves.
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r2.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، عن وهب بن منبه، {لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس} [طه: 10] قال: بقبس تصطلون

TAB-FULL:v16p20/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r3.claim: Seeking guidance at the fire means seeking someone to direct them along the lost road, or information and knowledge that would reveal the way.
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r3.anchor: دلالة تدل على الطريق الذي أضللناه

TAB-FULL:v16p20/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada explain the hoped-for guidance as a person who can show the road; Qatada also reports an attribution to Ibn Abbas that the place was Aylah.
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r4.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {أو أجد على النار هدى} [طه: 10] يقول: من يدل على الطريق

TAB-FULL:v16p20/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r5.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r5.claim: Wahb interprets the guidance as knowledge of the route, learned from an account describing the way.
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r5.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه، {أو أجد على النار هدى} [طه: 10] قال: هدى عن علم الطريق

TAB-FULL:v16p20/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r6.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r6.claim: Ikrima reports Ibn Abbas saying they had lost the route and hoped either to find a guide or bring back a firebrand for warmth.
TAB-FULL:v16p20/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد، عن عكرمة، قال: قال ابن عباس {لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس أو أجد على النار هدى} [طه: 10]

ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r3.claim: قبس is a brand taken from the tip of a stick or from a wick.
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r3.anchor: القبس ما أخذته في رأس. عود من النار أو رأس فتيلة.

ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r4.claim: Tafsir says Moses had lost the road, or was away from water, and hoped to find someone by the fire to guide him to the road or water.
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r4.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ضل الطريق وجاء أنه ضل عن الماء فرجا أن يجد عند النار من يهديه الطريق

TABATABAI:20:9-12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:9-12/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:9-12/r4.claim: Makath means stay; ānasa means seeing or finding, strongly perceiving something familiar; qabas is a flame carried on a stick, and hudā means guidance or a guide.
TABATABAI:20:9-12/r4.anchor: المكث اللبث، والإيناس إبصار الشيء أو وجدانه

TABATABAI:20:9-12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:9-12/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:9-12/r5.claim: Moses was returning from Midian toward Egypt on a cold dark night with his family near Tuwa in Sinai; they had lost the road, so he went toward the fire to ask directions or bring back a flame for warmth.
TABATABAI:20:9-12/r5.anchor: كان في منصرفه من مدين إلى مصر ومعه أهله وهم بالقرب من وادي طوى

TABATABAI:20:9-12/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:9-12/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:9-12/r6.claim: His instruction to stay indicates others were with his family; the emphatic report that he alone perceived a fire indicates that the others did not see it, and an omitted clause means he would go and return with flame or a guide.
TABATABAI:20:9-12/r6.anchor: مع ما يشتمل عليه من التأكيد والتعبير بالإيناس دلالة على أنه إنما رآها هو وحده

TABRISI:20:9-16/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-16/r2.speaker: حمزة
TABRISI:20:9-16/r2.claim: Hamza reads li-ahlihi umkuthū with a ḍamma on the hāʾ, also in al-Qaṣaṣ; others use kasra.
TABRISI:20:9-16/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة لأهله امكثوا وفي القصص أيضا بضم الهاء

TABRISI:20:9-12/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-12/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:9-12/r1.claim: Akhfaytu can mean either concealed or revealed, while khafaytuhu without the alif means only revealed; radā means destruction, as does taraddā.
TABRISI:20:9-12/r1.anchor: ويقال أخفيت الشيء كتمته وأظهرته جميعا وخفيته بلا ألف أظهرته لا غير

TABRISI:20:9-12/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-12/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:9-12/r2.claim: The verb idh raʾā is an accusative circumstantial phrase attached to an omitted word, describing the account of Moses.
TABRISI:20:9-12/r2.anchor: إذ رأى الظرف يتعلق بمحذوف فهو في موضع النصب على الحال من حديث موسى

TABRISI:20:9-12/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-12/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:9-12/r3.claim: Moses was jealous and avoided traveling companions; after finishing his term he left Midian with sheep, lost the dark route, his flock scattered, his fire striker failed, and his pregnant wife went into labor as he saw a distant fire.
TABRISI:20:9-12/r3.anchor: وكان موسى رجلا غيورا لا يصحب الرفقة لئلا ترى امرأته فلما قضى الأجل وفارق مدين خرج

TABRISI:20:9-12/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-12/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:9-12/r4.claim: Moses' wife was Shuʿayb's daughter, whom he had married in Midian.
TABRISI:20:9-12/r4.anchor: وهي بنت شعيب كان تزوجها بمدين

TABRISI:20:9-12/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-12/r5.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:20:9-12/r5.claim: It was a cold winter Friday night; iqāma is enduring, whereas makth is temporary.
TABRISI:20:9-12/r5.anchor: وكانت ليلة الجمعة في الشتاء والفرق بين المكث والإقامة أن الإقامة تدوم والمكث لا يدوم

TABRISI:20:9-12/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-12/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:9-12/r6.claim: Ānastu means I saw the fire, and Moses sought a flame from its great fire to warm his family.
TABRISI:20:9-12/r6.anchor: بشعلة اقتبسها من معظم النار تصطلون بها

TABRISI:20:9-12/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-12/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:9-12/r7.claim: Finding guidance by the fire means finding someone there to show the way; alternatively it means a sign for the route, and hudā names both guidance and what guides.
TABRISI:20:9-12/r7.anchor: أي أجد على النار هاديا يدلني على الطريق

TABRISI:20:9-12/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-12/r8.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:20:9-12/r8.claim: The fire could point to a guide because a fire is never without people nearby.
TABRISI:20:9-12/r8.anchor: لأن النار لا تخلو من أهل لها وناس عندها

TABRISI:20:9-12/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-12/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:9-12/r9.claim: As Moses approached, the fire appeared in a jujube tree; its brilliant light and vivid green amazed him before the tree called him.
TABRISI:20:9-12/r9.anchor: فإذا النار في شجرة عناب فوقف متعجبا من حسن ضوء تلك النار وشدة خضرة تلك الشجرة

THALABI:v6p239#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p239#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v6p239#2/r1.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports the Prophet saying Moses’ sandals were made from the hide of a dead donkey; another report says the hide was untanned.
THALABI:v6p239#2/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله فاخلع نعليك قال: كانتا من جلد حمار ميت

THALABI:v6p239#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p239#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v6p239#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan answers why Moses removed his sandals although Muhammad prayed in sandals: Moses’ sandals were made from donkey hide.
THALABI:v6p239#2/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: ما بال خلع النعلين في الصلاة وصلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في نعليه؟

THALABI:v6p239#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p239#2/r3.speaker: أبو الأحوص
THALABI:v6p239#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Ahwas recounts Ibn Mas'ud yielding the prayer lead to Abu Musa, who removed his sandals; Ibn Mas'ud joked, ‘Are you in the sacred valley?’
THALABI:v6p239#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو الأحوص: أتى عبد الله أبا موسى في داره فأقيمت الصلاة

THALABI:v6p239#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p239#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
THALABI:v6p239#2/r4.claim: Ikrima and Mujahid say Moses removed his sandals so his feet touched the blessed earth and received its blessing, sanctified twice.
THALABI:v6p239#2/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة ومجاهد: إنما قال له: اخلع نعليك كي تمس راحة قدميك الأرض الطيبة

THALABI:v6p239#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p239#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p239#2/r5.claim: Other explanations say barefootedness marks humility, allows the heels to receive the valley’s blessing, or symbolizes emptying one’s heart of family and children; shoes in dreams signify a wife.
THALABI:v6p239#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم: أمر بذلك لأن الحفوة من أمارات التواضع

ASAD-NOTES:20:9#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:9#n7/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:9#n7/r1.claim: Because the sequence also appears in 27:7 and 28:29, Asad thinks Moses was lost in the desert; this may symbolize his dawning need for spiritual guidance.
ASAD-NOTES:20:9#n7/r1.anchor: Moses had lost his way in the desert: probably a symbolic allusion to his dawning awareness that he was in need of spiritual guidance

ASAD-NOTES:20:9#n7/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:9#n7/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:9#n7/r2.claim: This episode belongs to Moses’ wanderings after his flight from Egypt, as described from 28:14 onward.
ASAD-NOTES:20:9#n7/r2.anchor: the period of his wanderings subsequent to his flight from Egypt (see 28:14 ff.)

ASAD-NOTES:20:9#n7/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:9#n7/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:9#n7/r3.claim: Asad treats the fire as an allegory of the Bible’s burning bush and refers to his note on 27:7-8.
ASAD-NOTES:20:9#n7/r3.anchor: the allegory of the "fire" - the "burning bush" of the Bible - see note 7 on 27:7-8

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p362/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p362/r1.speaker: وهب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p362/r1.claim: Moses obtained Shuʿayb’s leave to return to his parents; on a snowy, bitter night his wife bore a son, they lost the road, his fire-making failed, and he glimpsed fire off to the left.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p362/r1.anchor: وهب: (استأذن موسى عليه السلام شعيبا (¬7) بالرجوع إلى والديه فأذن له، فخرج بأهله فولد له ابن في الطريق # في ليلة شاتية مثلجة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p362/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p362/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p362/r2.claim: Moses was jealous and avoided traveling with a group so they would not see his wife; on a dark night he lost the way and saw distant fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p362/r2.anchor: عطاء عن ابن عباس: (كان موسى رجلا غيورا لا يصحب الرفقة لئلا ترى امرأته، فأخطأ الطريق في ليلة مظلمة فرأى نارا من بعيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p362/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p362/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p362/r3.claim: The family addressed was Moses’s wife, Shuʿayb’s daughter; although the address is singular, ahl can denote a group, as in ahl al-bayt, so the wording uses the broader outward form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p362/r3.anchor: يريد امرأته بنت شعيب {امكثوا} أقيموا مكانكم، الخطاب لامرأته ولكنه خرج على ظاهر لفظ الأهل، فإن الأهل يقع على الجماعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r1.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r1.claim: Anasa describes seeing something distant that reassures or comforts the observer; the root also describes a hunting bird noticing prey.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r1.anchor: المبرد: (ويقول الذي يبصر الشيء من بعيد مما تسكن إليه نفسه: آنست كذا أي رأيته لي أنسا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r2.speaker: العجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r2.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj’s line illustrates the lexical use of the word anisa.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r3.claim: The commentators gloss anastu simply as I saw or perceived.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r4.claim: Qabas is a flame taken from a larger fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r4.anchor: القبس: شعلة من نار يقتبسها من معظم النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r5.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r5.claim: Abu Zayd distinguishes forms for imparting knowledge and bringing fire: the unprefixed verb is used for bringing fire, while the prefixed form is used when seeking it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r5.anchor: أبو زيد: (أقبست الرجل علما بالألف، وقبسته نارا إذا جئته بها، فإن كان طلبها قال: أقبسته بالألف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r6.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r6.claim: Al-Kisāʾī allows both prefixed and unprefixed forms for fire or knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r6.anchor: الكسائي: (أقبسته نارا وعلما سواء، وقد يجوز طرح الألف منهما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r7.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r7.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the two forms have one underlying sense because both fire and knowledge provide illumination.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p363/r7.anchor: والأصل واحدة لأن كلاهما مستضاء به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r1.claim: Hudan means someone who points out the road.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r2.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r2.claim: Hudan means a guide who directs travelers along the road.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains hudan, a verbal noun, as used in place of the personal noun hādiyan, a guide.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj understands Moses to hope to find someone by the fire who would guide him on the road.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r4.anchor: رجاء أن يجد عند النار من يهديه للطريق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r5.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r5.claim: Al-Suddī reasons that the fire must have people associated with it, since a fire is not without people who tend or gather around it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365/r5.anchor: لأن النار لا تخلو من أهل لها وناس عندها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:9-14/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:9-14/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:9-14/r2.claim: On the way to Egypt, while his wife was in labor, Moses saw what looked like fire and told her to wait; he hoped to bring a flame or find a guide because he had lost the road.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:9-14/r2.anchor: في طريقه إلى مصر لما أخذ امرأته الطلق

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r2.claim: Moses saw what seemed to him fire, though it was actually light; “I saw a fire” means he saw a light, according to al-Suddi.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r3.claim: Moses hoped for a flame to warm his family, as another verse says, since it was winter; here he also hoped to find a guide to the road.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r4.claim: “Guidance” means people who would show Moses the road.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r5.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r5.claim: “Guidance” means someone to direct him along the road.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253#2/r6.claim: Moses was off the road, walking in reliance on his Lord without knowing the way.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r3.claim: Other Qur’anic passages indicate Moses was traveling from Midian to Egypt with his family after working for his father-in-law for eight or ten years.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r3.anchor: Hz. Mûsâ’nın Medyen’de sekiz (veya on) yıl kayınpederinin yanında çalıştıktan sonra ailesiyle birlikte Mısır’a gitmek üzere yola çıktığı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r4.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r4.claim: Exegetes say this occurred on a cold winter night when Moses had lost his way and saw a light that he thought was fire; its significance was to lead him into the divine presence.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r4.anchor: Tefsirlerde bu olayın soğuk bir kış gecesinde ve Mûsâ’nın yolunu kaybettiği bir sırada meydana geldiği

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p4/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p4/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p4/r7.claim: The account of Moses begins with his return from Midian to the sacred valley of Ṭuwā, where he receives prophethood.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r5.claim: Moses encountered the flame while returning from Midian with his family.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r6.claim: Moses saw only a brief, shimmering flame, perhaps unseen by anyone else, rather than a large fire.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r6.anchor: not seen a big fire burning but only some sort of a flame which shimmered and then disappeared

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r7.claim: The verb ʾānasa came to mean seeing and observing intently.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r7.anchor: this word also began to be used to mean “to see and observe intently.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r8.claim: If it had been a blazing fire, Moses would have said it burned at a distance and gone to seek directions or bring back an ember against the cold.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r8.anchor: that a fire was burning at a distance

IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r2.speaker: حمزة، ابن سعدان عن إسحق المسيبي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r2.claim: They read لأهله امكثوا with ḍamma on hāʾ in both 20:10 and 28:29; the others use kasra.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة وابن سعدان عن إسحق المسيبى ﴿ لأهله امكثوا ﴾

QIRAAT-ER:20:10:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:10:7#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:20:10:7#1/r1.claim: The pronoun suffix in li-ahlihu has ḍamma instead of kasra; the source suggests dialectal leveling or a different syntactic analysis.
QIRAAT-ER:20:10:7#1/r1.anchor: Nominative -hu instead of genitive -hi on pronoun suffix; Abu Jaʿfar and others

QIRAAT-ER:20:10:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:10:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:20:10:9#1/r1.claim: The first-person yāʾ is open in inniya rather than quiescent in innī, changing prosody without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:20:10:9#1/r1.anchor: Open yāʾ (inniya) vs. quiescent yāʾ (innī) — a phonological variant

QIRAAT-ER:20:10:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:10:12#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:20:10:12#1/r1.claim: The yāʾ in laʿalliya is open rather than quiescent, paralleling the inniya variant and leaving the meaning unchanged.
QIRAAT-ER:20:10:12#1/r1.anchor: Open yāʾ (laʿalliya) vs. quiescent yāʾ (laʿallī) — phonological variant

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#3/r1.claim: Qatada interprets Moses’ hope for guidance by the fire as hoping to find someone to show him the road.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ أو أجد على النار هدى ﴾ قال من يهديني الطريق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r3.claim: Ānasa means to find or perceive; a qabas is an ember carried on a stick, and the root also applies metaphorically to acquired knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r3.anchor: آنس: وجد، تقول العرب: هل آنست فلان أي وجدته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r4.claim: Al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza’s verse uses ānasa for sensing a faint sound.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r4.anchor: آنست نبأة وروعها القناص ... عصرا وقد دنا الإمساء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r5.speaker: المبرد والكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad distinguishes giving knowledge from fire; al-Kisāʾī allows the same verbs with either.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r5.anchor: وقال المبرد: أقبست الرجل علم وقبسته نارا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r7.claim: Saʿy means swift movement or action; radā is to perish and ardā to destroy; Durayd ibn al-Ṣimma’s poem illustrates the latter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r7.anchor: ردي يردى ردى هلك، وأرداه أهلكه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314/r5.claim: Moses completed the longer term, asked Shuʿayb to return to Egypt, then traveled in winter with his pregnant wife through an unknown route.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314/r5.anchor: لما قضى أكمل الأجلين استأذن شعيبا في الرجوع من مدين إلى مصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314/r6.claim: In a dark, freezing night his wife’s labor began and his firesteel failed to spark.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314/r6.anchor: في ليلة مظلمة مثلجة شديدة البرد، وأخذ امرأته الطلق فقدح زنده فلم يور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r1.claim: One account says Moses avoided exposing his wife by joining a caravan at night and leaving by day, which caused him to lose the route.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r1.anchor: قيل: كان رجلا غيورا يصحب الرفقة ليلا ويفارقهم نهارا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r2.speaker: وهب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r2.claim: Wahb says Moses’s son was born on the road; when his firesteel hardened, he saw a fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r2.anchor: قال وهب: ولد له ابن في الطريق ولما صلد زنده رأى نارا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r3.claim: Idh is apparently an adverb attached to Moses’s account; al-Zamakhsharī also permits an omitted description or makes it the object of udhkur.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن إذ ظرف للحديث لأنه حدث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r4.claim: Amkuthū means stay in place; Moses addresses his wife, two sons, and servant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r4.anchor: امكثوا أي أقيموا في مكانكم، وخاطب امرأته وولديه والخادم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r5.speaker: الأعمش وطلحة وحمزة ونافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r5.claim: They read li-ahlihi umkuthū with ḍamma on hāʾ; the majority reads with kasra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وطلحة وحمزة ونافع في رواية لأهله امكثوا بضم الهاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r6.claim: Ānasa means perceived; since the fire was far away and seen by sight, some gloss it as “saw,” though the word is broader.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r6.anchor: إني آنست أي أحسست، والنار على بعد لا تحس إلا بالبصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī defines īnās as clear, unambiguous seeing; Moses uses laʿalla because the ember or guidance was hoped for, not certain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r7.anchor: الإيناس الإبصار البين الذي لا شبهة فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r8.speaker: الماوردي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r8.claim: Al-Māwardī says it was fire for Moses but light for God; Abū Ḥayyān rejects the view that Moses only imagined fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r8.anchor: وقال الماوردي: كانت عند موسى نارا وكانت عند الله نورا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r9.claim: ʿAlā retains its ordinary “above/on” sense; Ibn al-Anbārī also allows “at,” “with,” or “by.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r9.anchor: ولفظة على هاهنا على بابها من الاستعلاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r10.speaker: الزجاج ومجاهد وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj says Moses sought someone to guide him to route or water; Mujāhid and Qatāda say hudā means religious guidance, which the author calls remote.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r10.anchor: وذكر الزجاج أنه ضل عن الماء فترجى أن يلقى من يهديه الطريق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r11.claim: Hudā is an object with an omitted possessor, “someone with guidance,” or an ellipsis because finding a guide is finding guidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p314#2/r11.anchor: وانتصب هدى على أنه مفعول به على تقدير محذوف أي ذا هدى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعبد الله ووهب وقتادة ومقاتل والكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r1.claim: Authorities identify the fire-bearing tree as ʿanāb, samura, ʿawsaj, or ʿalīqah; the fire receded when Moses approached.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r1.anchor: في شجرة خضراء يانعة عناب قاله ابن عباس. وقيل: سمرة قاله عبد الله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r1.claim: The time clause most plausibly attaches to the preceding noun for the revealed discourse, not to that noun if it simply means speech, since a substantive cannot govern it; telling the story is more fitting than describing its telling.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r1.anchor: والاظهر أنه اسم لما ذكر لأنه هو المعروف مع أن وصف القصة بالاتيان أولى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r2.speaker: الشريف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r2.claim: Al-Sharif transmits that story, account, report, and news may govern adverbial clauses even without a verbal meaning because they imply occurrence.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r2.anchor: نقل الشريف عن بعضهم أن القصة والحديث والخبر والنبا يجوز اعمالها في الظروف خاصة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r3.claim: Other parses make the clause modify an omitted later event or an omitted earlier command to remember the time Musa saw the fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ظرفا لمضمر مؤخر أي حين رأى نارا كان كيت وكيت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r4.claim: One report says Musa asked Shuayb to leave Midian for Egypt to visit his mother and brother after a long absence, hoping the old case would be forgotten; Shuayb permitted him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r4.anchor: استاذن شعيبا عليه السلام في الخروج من مدين إلى مصر لزيارة امه واخيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r5.claim: Musa was jealous and traveled with his family without a caravan so his wife would not be seen; she rode a donkey with household goods while he drove sheep and avoided the usual road for fear of Syrian rulers.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r5.anchor: وكان عليه السلام رجلا غيورا فخرج بأهله ولم يصحب رفقة لئلا ترى امرأته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r6.claim: At Wadi Tuwa west of the mountain, on a dark snowy Friday night, his wife bore a son; Musa had lost the way, his flock had scattered, there was no water, and his flint would not spark before he saw fire to the left.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r6.anchor: ولد له ابن في ليلة مظلمة شاتية مثلجة وكانت ليلة الجمعه وقد ضل الطريق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r7.claim: Musa tells his family to stay so they will not follow him to the fire as people commonly do, not because he fears they will relocate elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r7.anchor: أمرهم عليه السلام بذلك لئلا يتبعوه فيما عزم عليه من الذهاب إلى النار

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r8.claim: The plural address may include wife, child, and servant, or the wife alone, with plural explained by the word family or by honorific usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165/r8.anchor: والخطاب قيل : للمرأة والولد والخادم وقيل : للمرأة وحدها والجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r1.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r1.claim: Al-A'mash, Talha, Hamza, and one transmission from Nafi read the hāʾ in li-ahli as damma.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وطلحة وحمزة ونافع في رواية ( ﴿ لأهله امكثوا ﴾ ) بضم الهاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r2.claim: Anastu means seeing something clearly and without doubt; related explanations connect it with the eye's pupil, the opposite of jinn, reassuring sight, or simply finding something.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r2.anchor: أي ابصرتها ابصارا بينا لا شبهة فيه ومن ذلك انسان العين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r3.speaker: الحارث بن حلزة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r3.claim: Al-Harith ibn Hilliza's line uses anastu to witness the sense of noticing or seeing.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r3.anchor: قال الحرث بن حلزة : آنست نبأة وقد راعها القن اص يوما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r4.claim: The statement explains both the command and its content; inna confirms the certain sight to reassure his family, although they had shown neither doubt nor denial.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r4.anchor: والجملة تعليل للأمر والمامور به ولما كان الايناس مقطوعا متيقنا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r5.claim: A qabas is a flame carried on the end of a stick, a passive form meaning something kindled; it is the same as a flame-brand and the jadwah elsewhere, not an ember.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r5.anchor: بشعلة مقتبسة تكون على رأس عود ونحوه ففعل بمعنى مفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows min-ha to attach directly to the verb or to an omitted circumstantial phrase describing the firebrand.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r7.claim: Guidance may mean a guide to the path, a verbal noun used for its agent, a guide possessing guidance by ellipsis, or simply guidance metonymically for finding a guide.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r7.anchor: هاديا يدلنى على الطريق على أنه مصدر سمى به الفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Musa wanted someone to guide him to water, since he had lost it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r8.anchor: وعن الزجاج أن المراد هاديا يدلنى على الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r9.claim: Mujahid and Qatada interpret guidance as direction to the paths of religion, since the minds of the righteous remain occupied with religious purposes; al-Alusi calls this far-fetched given the family-consoling narrative and the parallel wording in 28:29.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p165#2/r9.anchor: وعن مجاهد وقتادة أن المراد هاديا يهدينى إلى ابواب الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r1.claim: Abu al-Baqa prefers spelling hudan with alif and no imala; those who incline it explain it by tanwin resembling a lexical ending, by retaining the lexical ending without tanwin, or by a pausal form used in all cases.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r1.anchor: الجيد أن تكتب بالالف ولا تمال لا الالف بدل التنوين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r2.claim: Aw prevents exclusion rather than combining both possibilities; ala retains its basic sense of elevation, which became idiomatic for a nearby place close beside the fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r2.anchor: وكلمة أو لمنع الخلو دون الجمع وعل على بابها من الاستعلاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r3.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r3.claim: Sibawayh explains the preposition bi in marartu bi-Zayd as contact with a place close to him, supporting the local use of ala.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r3.anchor: كما قال سيبويه في مررت بزيد : أنه لصوق بمكان يقرب منه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r4.claim: Some grammarians treat the phrase as a circumstantial description of a guide, moved before its noun: a guide or guidance near the fire, meaning someone to help them warm themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r4.anchor: وقال غير واحد : أن الجار والمجرور في موقع الحال من ( هدى )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r5.speaker: الأنباري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r5.claim: Al-Anbari proposes that ala means at, with, or by, but the author sees no need for these substitutions.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r5.anchor: وعن الأنبارى أن على ههنا بمعنى عند أو بمعنى مع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r6.claim: The verse names the fire rather than using a pronoun to explain why guidance might be found there, since people are commonly present around a fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r6.anchor: وصدرت الجملة بكلمة الترجى لما أن الآيتان وما عطف عليه ليسا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r7.claim: The expression of hope reflects two anticipated possibilities, not certain outcomes; syntactically it may be a rationale for the command, the subject's state as he goes, or an adjective of fire, though the last is rejected.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r7.anchor: أما علة لفعل قد حذف ثقة بما يدل عليه من الأمر بالمكث

ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r8.claim: Treating the whole clause of hope as an adjective of fire is defended by comparison to a poetic line, but the author says the analysis is flawed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p166/r8.anchor: وقيل : هى صفة لنارا ومتى جاز جعل جملة الترجى صلة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r1.claim: Moses asked Shuayb to return from Midian to Egypt to visit his mother and sister; Shuayb allowed him to leave with family and possessions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r1.anchor: استأذن شعيبا في الرجوع من مدين إلى مصر لزيارة والدته وأخته، فأذن له فخرج بأهله وماله،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r2.claim: One account says winter travel on a detour to avoid Syrian rulers; Moses's wife was ill, they lost their way in a freezing dark night, she went into labor, and his flint would not spark.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r2.anchor: وكانت أيام الشتاء، وأخذ على غير الطريق مخافة ملوك الشام، وامرأته في سقمها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r3.claim: Another account says Moses, jealous over his wife, traveled with caravans at night and apart by day; lost on a cold dark night, he saw fire after his flint failed, as God intended to honor him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r3.anchor: وقيل: إن موسى كان رجلا غيورا فكان يصحب الرفقة بالليل ويفارقهم بالنهار،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r4.claim: Amkuthu means stay or remain; Hamza reads the hā with damma here and in al-Qasas.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r4.anchor: أقيموا، قرأ حمزة بضم الهاء هاهنا وفي القصص،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r5.claim: Anastu means I saw; a qabs is a flame or piece of fire carried on a stick from a larger fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r5.anchor: {إني آنست} أي: أبصرت، {نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس} شعلة من نار،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r6.claim: Hudan means someone at the fire who can guide Moses to the road.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r6.anchor: {أو أجد على النار هدى} أي: أجد عند النار من يدلني على الطريق.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r7.claim: At the fire Moses saw a green tree surrounded from bottom to top by brilliant white fire, neither changing the other's color or light.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r7.anchor: رأى شجرة خضراء من أسفلها [إلى أعلاها، أطافت بها نار بيضاء تتقد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r8.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the tree as a green samura.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r8.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: كانت الشجرة سمرة خضراء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r9.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r9.claim: Qatada, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi identify the tree as al-awsaj.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة، ومقاتل، والكلبي: كانت من العوسج.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r10.speaker: وهب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r10.claim: Wahb identifies the tree as al-aliq.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r11.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas identifies the tree as a jujube tree.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r11.anchor: شجرة العناب، روي ذلك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r12.speaker: أهل التفسير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r12.claim: The exegetes say Moses saw light rather than fire; it is called fire because he thought it was fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r12.anchor: قال أهل التفسير: لم يكن الذي رآه موسى نارا بل كان نورا، ذكر بلفظ النار لأن موسى حسبه نارا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r13.claim: Most exegetes, including Ibn Abbas and Ikrima, say it was the light of the Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r13.anchor: وقال أكثر المفسرين: إنه نور الرب عز وجل، وهو قول ابن عباس، وعكرمة، وغيرهما.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r14.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says it was actual fire and one of God's veils; a report from Abu Musa says the fire veil would burn creation as far as God's sight reaches if lifted.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p265/r14.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هي النار بعينها، وهي إحدى حجب الله تعالى،

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r1.claim: Idh is an adverb attached to the account as an event, or the object of a command to remember.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r1.anchor: ظرف لل { حديث } لأنه حدث أو مفعول لأذكر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r2.claim: One account says Moses asked Jethro to visit his mother, then traveled with family; on a dark, snowy Friday near Tuwa his son was born, he lost the way and livestock, and saw fire by the mountain.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r2.anchor: قيل إنه استأذن شعيبا عليهما الصلاة والسلام في الخروج إلى أمه، وخرج بأهله فلما وافى وادي طوى

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r3.claim: Amkuthū means stay; Hamza reads hāhunā after ahl and uses ḍamma on hāʾ in connected speech in al-Qasas, unlike others.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r3.anchor: فقال لأهله امكثوا } أقيموا مكانكم. وقرأ حمزة «لأهله امكثوا ها هنا»، وفي «القصص» بضم الهاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r4.claim: Ānastu means seeing clearly without doubt, or seeing what brings familiarity; qabas means a flame or ember, and hudā means a guide or religious guidance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r4.anchor: إني آنست نارا } أبصرتها إبصارا لا شبهة فيه، وقيل الإيناس إبصار ما يؤنس به. { لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس }

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r5.claim: Moses expresses hope for fire and guidance because they might follow sighting, but reports the sighting with certainty so his family can prepare; ʿalā may mean above the fire or nearby elevated ground.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:10/r5.anchor: ولما كان حصولهما مترتبا بني الأمر فيهما على الرجاء بخلاف الإيناس، فإنه كان محققا ولذلك حققه لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r1.claim: The second coherence reading is stronger: creation belongs to God, and a divinely aided person can face no difficult task; Moses's rescue, Pharaoh's destruction, and Israel's emergence reinforce this point.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r1.anchor: وهذا الوجه الثاني أولى من الأول - والله أعلم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r2.claim: Returning from Midian, Moses clearly saw a fire in the dark and told his family to stay; anastu denotes seeing plainly, and he hoped to bring a glowing brand for warmth or find guidance on the hidden road.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r2.anchor: أي أبصرت في هذا الظلام إبصارا بينا لا شبهة فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r3.claim: A qabas is a flame carried on the tip of a stick, useful against the cold; hudā means guidance because the path had become hidden.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r3.anchor: أي بشعلة من النار في رأس حطبة فيها جمرة تعين

TABATABAI:20:47-48/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r11.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r11.claim: A report from Imam al-Bāqir says the firebrand was for warmth in the cold, and Moses hoped to find a road because he had lost his way.
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r11.anchor: في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { آتيكم منها بقبس } يقول آتيكم بقبس من النار

BAQILLANI:v1p189/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p189/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p189/r1.claim: The Moses fire episode is told in varied forms across Ṭā Hā, al-Naml, and al-Qaṣaṣ; this range of narrative expression makes the challenge to produce a comparable discourse more comprehensive.
BAQILLANI:v1p189/r1.anchor: لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس أو أجد على النار هدى

BAQILLANI:v1p189/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p189/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p189/r3.claim: Every word is beautiful and meaningful on its own, while the words become still more impressive through their precise arrangement and the smooth transitions between stories and sections.
BAQILLANI:v1p189/r3.anchor: كل كلمة لو أفردت كانت في الجمال غاية وفي الدلالة آية فكيف إذا قارنتها أخواتها

BAQILLANI:v1p189/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p189/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p189/r4.claim: A skilled writer can test the claim by paraphrasing one Qurʾānic story and comparing the obvious loss in the substitute wording.
BAQILLANI:v1p189/r4.anchor: فإن كنت من أهل الصنعة فاعمد إلى قصة من هذه القصص وحديث من هذه الأحاديث

BURHAN:v1p130/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p130/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p130/r9.claim: Ṭā Hā says فلما أتاها, while al-Naml says فلما جاءها.
BURHAN:v1p130/r9.anchor: فى طه ﴿ فلما أتاها ﴾ وفى النمل ﴿ فلما جاءها ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p438/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p438/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p438/r6.anchor: امكثوا اى انزلوا . قوله سبحانه فى سورة طه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r1.claim: In Joseph’s story, the king’s dream was true inspiration, not the confused dreams his court thought it was.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r1.anchor: فإذا رؤيا الملك صادقة الإلهام، وليست كما بدت للملأ من قومه أضغاث أحلام

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r2.claim: Dictionaries gloss ānasa as seeing an object or hearing a sound, and istaʾnasa as asking permission.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r2.anchor: في المعاجم، آنس الشيء أبصره، والصوتَ سمعه. واستأنس: استأذن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r3.claim: The author argues ānasa is not a neutral synonym for seeing or hearing: it implies finding familiarity or comfort in what is perceived.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r4.claim: Four Quranic uses concern Moses encountering fire, across these passages; the fifth is in the verse about discerning sound judgment in orphans.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p217/r4.anchor: والقرآن قد استعمل الفعل "آنس" خمس مرات

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r1.claim: The jinn passage about a guarded seat for hearing has a different context from the shihāb qabs Moses sought at the fire.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r1.anchor: وسياق آياتها، في الجن، غير سياق "شهابٍ قبسٍ"

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r2.claim: Qabs occurs again in this Moses passage, and the Quran also uses the verb iqtabasa for taking light from another’s light.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r2.anchor: وقد جاء "قَبس" مرة أخرى في السياق نفسه بآية طه 10

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r3.claim: A qabs is a flame taken from a larger fire; shihāb suggests a bright flare, and al-Raghib defines it as a bright flame from a fire or atmospheric phenomenon.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r3.anchor: ومن معاني القبس في اللغة: شعلة نار تقتبس من معظم النار

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r4.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r4.claim: Al-Raghib explains shihāb as a bright flame from a burning fire or a phenomenon in the sky.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r5.claim: Arabic usage also calls stars shuhub, a snow-covered mountain shihāb, and a streak of whiteness through blackness a shuhba.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r5.anchor: والشهب في العربية: الدرارى؛ والشهب، بفتحتين: الجبل علاه الثلج

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r7.claim: The author contrasts Moses’s qabs with hostile meteors: in Moses’s story shihāb appears with familiarity, guidance, and light, not a warning or expulsion.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r7.anchor: فوجهت كلمة "بشهاب" معها، إلى غير سياقها الرادع الزاجر

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r3.claim: The hāʾ in “li-ahlihi” is read with ḍamma or kasra; the author refers to the explanation in al-Baqara.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r3.anchor: يقرأبضم الهاء وكسرها وقد ذكرت علته في البقرة

NASHR:v2p165/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p165/r3.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p165/r3.claim: Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir, and Abu Jaʿfar use fatḥ on the final ya of لعلي in six occurrences across Yusuf, Taha, al-Muʾminun, al-Qasas, and Ghafir.
NASHR:v2p165/r3.anchor: واتفق نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبو جعفر على فتح لعلي حيث وقعت

NASHR:v2p322/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r5.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p322/r5.claim: For five yāʾs of annexation—إني آنست, إني أنا ربك, إنني أنا الله, لنفسي اذهب, and في ذكري—the two Medinese, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read the yāʾ open.
NASHR:v2p322/r5.anchor: إني آنست، إني أنا ربك، إنني أنا الله، لنفسي اذهب، في ذكري اذهبا

NASHR:v2p322/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r6.speaker: الكوفيون ويعقوب
NASHR:v2p322/r6.claim: The Kufans and Yaqub read the yāʾ of لعلي آتيكم quiescent.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ opens the listed first-person yāʾs except ولي فيها and أخي اشدد, where he uses sukūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.anchor: ففتحهن نافع إلا اثنتين قوله ﴿ ولي فيها مآرب ﴾ وقوله ﴿ أخي اشدد ﴾ فإنه أسكنهما

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr uses sukūn on ولي فيها and حشرتني أعمى, opening the other listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.anchor: وأسكن أبو عمرو منها اثنتين / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ لم حشرتني أعمى ﴾ وفتح سائرها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr uses sukūn on ولي فيها، ويسر لي أمري، لذكري إن، على عيني إذ, and برأسي إني; he opens the rest.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.anchor: وأسكن ابن كثير منها خمسا / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ ويسر لي أمري ﴾ و ﴿ لذكري إن ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، ابن عامر، عاصم عن أبي بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.claim: These readers use sukūn on all listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.anchor: وأسكنها كلها حمزة والكسائى وابن عامر وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر

DURR-FULL:v5p553/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r5.claim: Qatada explains ‘I perceive a fire’ as ‘I sense a fire,’ and seeking guidance there as asking who will guide him.
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {إني آنست نارا} أي أحسست نارا

DURR-FULL:v5p553/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses hoped someone would guide him to the road; he and his family were traveling in winter and had lost the way.
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - في قوله: {أو أجد على النار هدى} قال: من يهديني إلى الطريق

DURR-FULL:v5p553/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses the request as asking who would point out the road.
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {أو أجد على النار هدى} يقول: من يدل على الطريق

DURR-FULL:v5p553/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r8.speaker: مجاهد
