DURR-FULL:v5p553/r8.claim: Mujahid says Moses sought someone to guide him along the road.
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {أو أجد على النار هدى} قال: يهديه الطريق

DURR-FULL:v5p553/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r9.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r9.claim: Ikrima says Moses sought a guide who would lead him to water.
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r9.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله: {أو أجد على النار هدى} قال: هاد يهديني إلى الماء

DURR-FULL:v5p553/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r10.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r10.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih describes Moses seeing a great fire within the green al-‘aliq tree: it kept growing without consuming the lush tree, then retreated and went out when Moses tried to take a flame.
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r10.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه قال: لما رأى موسى النار انطلق يسير حتى وقف منها قريبا فإذا هو بنار عظيمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r5.claim: Idh is an adverb attached to the story; the sight of fire allows many scenarios and heightens suspense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r5.anchor: وإذ } ظرف للحديث . وقد تقدم نظائره ، وخص هذا الظرف بالذكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r6.claim: Seeing fire indicates night and that Moses needed fire, explaining his instruction to his family to wait.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r6.anchor: ورؤية النار تدل على أن ذلك كان بليل ، وأنه كان بحاجة إلى النار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r7.claim: Ahl means his wife and children; the plural command confirms they were with him, and Exodus also says Moses traveled with wife and sons on donkeys toward Egypt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r7.anchor: والأهل : الزوج والأولاد . وكانوا معه بقرينة الجمع في قوله { امكثوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r8.speaker: حمزة وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r8.claim: The majority read the hāʾ in ahlihi with kasra; Ḥamza and Khalaf read it with ḍamma, assimilating to the following hamzat al-waṣl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بكسر هاء ضمير أهله على الأصل . وقرأه حمزة وخلف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r9.claim: Īnās is seeing clearly, without uncertainty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r9.anchor: والإيناس : الإبصار البين الذي لا شبهة فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r10.claim: The emphatic inna signals the importance of good news to his family in darkness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r10.anchor: وتأكيد الخبر بإن لقصد الاهتمام به بشارة لأهله إذ كانوا في الظلمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r11.claim: Qabas is a flame or ember taken from a burning source, such as a coal or firebrand; this implies darkness and no means to kindle fire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r11.anchor: والقبس : ما يؤخذ اشتعاله من اشتعال شيء ويقبس ، كالجمرة من مجموع الجمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r12.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r12.claim: An alternative says Moses tried to strike a spark with his flint, but it failed to catch.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r12.anchor: وقيل : اقتدح زنده فصلد ، أي لم يقدح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r13.claim: Finding guidance by the fire means finding someone who knows the route and is traveling in the same direction, so he can guide Moses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r13.anchor: ومعنى أو أجد على النار هدى } : أو ألقى عارفا بالطريق قاصدا السير فيما أسير فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r14.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r14.claim: One explanation says Moses had lost the road in intense darkness and wanted to travel by night.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p193/r14.anchor: قيل : كان موسى قد خفي عليه الطريق من شدة الظلمة وكان يحب أن يسير ليلا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r1.claim: Aw expresses a choice: taking a flame is certain, while he might also find and accompany someone who knows the route.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r1.anchor: و { أو } هنا للتخيير ، لأن إتيانه بقبس أمر محقق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r2.claim: ʿAlā is figuratively spatial: it means very near the fire, as someone tends it for light or warmth; al-Aʿshā’s verse uses the same sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r2.anchor: وحرف { على } في قوله : { أو أجد على النار هدى } مستعمل في الاستعلاء المجازي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r3.speaker: الأعشى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r3.claim: Al-Aʿshā uses ʿalā with the sense of being close to the fire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r3.anchor:
قال الأعشى :
وبات على النار الندى والمحلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r4.claim: God inspired Moses to say hudā, anticipating that he would find great guidance at the fire and bring his people benefit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r4.anchor: وقد أجرى الله على لسان موسى معنى هذه الكلمة إلهاما إياه أنه سيجد عند تلك النار هدى عظيما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r5.claim: The fire is a subtle divine symbol: seeking light in darkness foreshadows revelation illuminating people with true religion after misguidance and false belief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r5.anchor: وإظهار النار لموسى رمز رباني لطيف ؛ إذ جعل اجتلابه لتلقي الوحي باستدعاء بنور في ظلمة
